title: Automatic recovery for suspended (WAL) tables on start-up
body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem?

When data is streamed to a table 24/7 and there is a power outage (or similar issue), upon resume of the server many (if not all) WAL tables are suspended due to corrupt data (I guess).

At this stage, the user needs to go an manually perform an `ALTER TABLE my_table RESUME WAL from txn 1231` 
Any corrupted transaction will not enter into the table, so the table will keep being suspended, unless this transaction is skipped. There is a lot of manual work or a separate script which the user needs to write in order to get the table back up and running.

It will be nice to have a feature where the user can say:
- i want each table to be auto resumed
- i want it to try and add any txn from WAL but skip the corrupted ones

### Describe the solution you'd like.

Manually resume the table 
or
manually resume WAL from the last transaction (essentially skipping all of them and discarding them)
or 
going one by one in the pending transaction until the table is fully caught up and resumed

### Describe alternatives you've considered.

Nothing else beyond what I wrote.

Either way I do not understand why a table will be suspended at all. Surely the user wants all possible good data from WAL to go into the table and the table to be back up and running. This can be automated, so the need for suspension at all is something I do not get why it exists and why it awaits user choice and intervention, since the rational choice (it seems) is always the same. 
I may be missing something.

### Full Name:

Stelian Nenkov

WA

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Hi @participant1, here's some context.

The table can become suspended for several reasons:

- database needs more RAM to execute the txn
- database needs more disk
- transaction cannot be applied (corrupted txn).

In the earlier two cases, the database deployment can be upgraded, and then the tables resumed. This is currently performed via [ALTER TABLE RESUME WAL](https://questdb.io/docs/reference/sql/alter-table-resume-wal/). I think the database may try to resume the tables on restart - if it doesn't, then it should, and you can add that.

In the case where the txn cannot be applied due to corruption, then it must be skipped. This is also done via a SQL command. 

In @reporter's case, he has a deployment which can be sometimes unstable, and encounters corrupted transactions. Rather than having to manually resume the table, he would like to skip as many transactions as is necessary to resume the table.

Places to start:

SqlCompilerImpl.alterTableResume
TableSequencerAPI.resumeTable

Those shows how tables can be resumed. 

The process to resume tables should be asynchronous and executed at startup. This can be implemented using the Task and Job APIs. Tasks can be found in `io.questdb.tasks` and you can search for the job process.

For testing, you can use an undocumented function, `ALTER TABLE table_name SUSPEND WAL`. You can also run this with a message on the end i.e `WITH "message"`. This requires you to add the `dev.mode.enabled` property to your `server.conf`.

For testing resuming corrupted transactions, you can suspend the table, then truncate or add garbage to the `_txn` file. This should be thoroughly tested.

Hope this helps!

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Some additional thoughts/ideas: When starting QuestDB, during the recovery process, it could check if the next transaction can be applied. If not, it could provide hints on what to do, for example, linking to https://questdb.io/docs/reference/sql/alter-table-resume-wal/.

Alternatively, there could be syntax like `ALTER TABLE <table> RESUME WAL FROM TRANSACTION AUTO;` or `ALTER TABLE <table> RESUME WAL FORCE`, where QuestDB would skip all transactions that cannot be applied. Obviously, this is a drastic option, but in practice, users would likely need to skip the problematic transactions manually anyway.

comments.author: participant6
comments.body:
@participant4 the result of power resets while running in non-sync durability mode can corrupt the main table storage. Then the only way is to restore the database from the backup. Sipping WAL transactions will not help in this case. It is also nearly impossible to detect that the database storage is corrupt unless everything is run in paranoia mode, checking every byte written.

If resuming the database by skipping WAL transactions after a power reset worked for you so far, consider yourself lucky.

If you want to run on unstable hardware there are only 2 choices:

- run in sync durability mode https://questdb.io/docs/concept/storage-model/#consistency-and-durability
- take snapshot/checkpoint every X minutes and on power reset, restore from the checkpoint https://questdb.io/docs/operations/backup/

The room for improvement can be:

- make durable mode less "taxing" on overall performance. It will use more CPU/IO however, that's given
- document how to make "cheaper" checkpoint copies where the files are stored on the same disk using hard links. This is only possible on LInux file systems.

The issue as it is stated cannot be solved, the database cannot always be restored after a power reset by skipping WAL transactions.
